title: Welcome to Chord Notepad
blocks: Chord Notepad is a text editor for musicians. Write a song the way a chord sheet looks: chords on their own line, right above the lyrics they go with.

C        C/E      F      C
Twinkle, twinkle, little star,
Dm    Am     G        C
How I wonder what you are!
The app recognizes chord lines on its own and highlights their chords; lyric lines are left alone. Click any chord in the editor to hear it, or press ▶ in the toolbar to play the whole song.

title: How Chord Lines Are Detected
blocks: There is nothing to mark up. A line counts as a chord line when most of its words are chords, so a lyric that happens to contain a word like “A” stays plain text.

G              D/F#        Em          C
A song for you, a melody I made
Am7   Dsus4   Cmaj7   G/B   F#m7b5   E7#9
Chords can be as rich as you need: sevenths, suspended and added notes, extensions, altered notes, and slash chords for a specific bass note.

title: Do-Re-Mi and Roman Numerals
blocks: Prefer solfège? Switch to European notation with the Do button in the toolbar and write chords as Do, Re, Mi… with a lowercase m for minor.

Do        Lam       Rem7      Sol7
Somewhere a melody is calling
Fa        Do/Mi     Rem       Sol
Every note is coming home
Roman numerals write chords relative to the key, set with {key: …} or the Key box. Change the key and the same song plays in the new key.

{key: G}
I         vi        IV        V7
Here's a tune in any key you like
ii7       V7        I
Play it high or play it low

title: Tempo, Meter and Timing
blocks: Directives in {braces} set the tempo, time signature and key. They can go anywhere, so a song can speed up or change key halfway through.

{bpm: 90} {time: 3/4}
G         G7        C*6
Walking slow in waltz time,
D7*1.5   C*1.5    G     NC
step and turn and home

Each chord lasts one bar unless you add *beats after it: C*6 holds for two bars of 3/4, D7*1.5 for a beat and a half. NC is a bar of silence. The toolbar's Speed, Key and Time controls set the defaults for the whole song.

title: Song Structure
blocks: Name a section with {label: …} and repeat it with {loop: name times}. Lines starting with // are comments: they're notes for you and are never played.
Tools → Insert has small dialogs for adding labels, loops and other directives if you'd rather not type them.

title: The Chord Sheet
blocks: The panel under the editor draws the song's chords as you write: as a piano roll, on a music staff, as guitar chord diagrams (Fret cards), or as tab. It follows along while the song plays.
Fret cards and Tab need a fretted instrument, picked in Playback → Voicing (for example Guitar). Show or hide the panel with View → Chord Sheet.

title: You're Ready!
blocks: That's all you need to get started.
Press F1 any time for the full User Guide (also in the Help menu). Tools → Identify Chord names a chord from the notes you pick, and Help → Quick Start brings this tour back.
